description: Troubleshooting procedure for faults during robotic placement of a single part into an indexing table fixture.

box_1.text: Does the part meet quality assurance team product specifications?

box_2.text: Check product dimensions and inspect for contamination.

box_3.text: Remove the non conforming parts and reload with a product batch that meets quality assurance team specifications.

box_4.text: Is picking up part from input slide correct?

box_5.text: Verification: parts must be centred under the vacuum end effectors and must not be dropped during transport. See input slide pickup diagnostic (GRAPH 17) if needed.

box_7.text: Is picking up part from reorientation mechanism correct?

box_8.text: Verification: parts must be centred under the vacuum end effectors and must not be dropped during transport. See reorientation mechanism placement diagnostic (GRAPH 19) if needed.

box_10.text: Is the setup of the indexing table correct?

box_11.text: Verify that there is no play between the setup tool and the indexing table during mounting (refer to the part mounting adjustment procedure). Then refer to the indexing table setup procedure.

box_14.text: Complete the following checks: 1. Check whether the vacuum end effectors are contaminated. 2. Check the vacuum filters for contamination. 3. Check whether the assembly robot axes are contaminated.

box_15.text: Pneumatic flow measurement procedure: vacuum flow check

box_16.text: Clean the parts, replace the vacuum filters, and replace the vacuum hose.

box_19.text: Complete the following checks: 1. Check cabling and upper displacement sensors on the vacuum end effectors. 2. Check whether the vacuum switches work correctly. 3. Check whether the valve for the vacuum generator works correctly. 4. Check system settings on the operator control interface.

box_20.text: Replace the defective cabling and/or displacement sensor on the vacuum end effectors.

box_22.text: Complete the following checks: 1. Check wear on the vacuum end effectors. 2. Check wear on the actuator grippers. 3. Check wear on the gripper pin through the aluminium block. 4. Check the assembly robot axes for wear.

box_23.text: Replace the worn components identified in the inspection (vacuum end effectors, actuator grippers, gripper pin, and/or assembly robot axes).

box_25.text: Is the z parallelism of the lower position of 4x gripper relative to each other correct?

box_26.text: Refer to the Z parallelism check for variant A machines (small format parts).

box_27.text: Refer to the Z parallelism check for variant B machines (medium format parts).

box_28.text: Refer to the Z parallelism check for variant C machines (large format parts).

box_29.text: Readjust the Z parallelism of the 4x gripper lower positions to the specified tolerance.

box_30.text: Is the part placement position in the indexing table correct?

box_31.text: Refer to the Z height and XY placement position check for variant A machines (small format parts).

box_32.text: Refer to the Z height and XY placement position check for variant B machines (medium format parts).

box_33.text: Refer to the Z height and XY placement position check for variant C machines (large format parts).

box_34.text: Pick up and placement adjustment procedure: part in indexing table

box_35.text: Perform assembly robot calibrations to correct the Z height and XY placement position into the indexing table fixture.

box_36.text: Restart this diagnostic procedure from the beginning.

box_37.text: Placing part in indexing table is correct
